english.title: Advertise / invite other to by unauthorised broadcast knowing / believing broadcast made by broadcasting station
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[advertised]_
(B)_[invited another, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), to advertise]_

by means of an unauthorised broadcast made by a broadcasting station from which unauthorised broadcasts were made, knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, that such broadcasts were made by the station
english.legislation: Contrary to section 38(2)(h) and (6) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 38(8) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that broadcasting station means a business or other operation (whether or not in the nature of a commercial venture) that is engaged in the making of broadcasts; and unauthorised broadcast means a broadcast made by means of the use of a wireless telegraphy station or wireless telegraphy apparatus in contravention of section 8 of the Act.
(ii) Section 38(4) of the Act provides that the cases in which a person is to be taken as advertising by means of a broadcast include any case in which he causes or allows it to be stated, suggested or implied that entertainment included in the broadcast has been supplied by him, or is wholly or partly at his expense.
(iii) Section 105 of the Act makes special provisions for this offence in relation to ships and aircraft.
(iv) Section 107 of the Act provides for proceedings and enforcement regarding this offence.
(v) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see paragraph 16(a) of Schedule 8 to the Act; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 35(2)(a) of the Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
